5. A first recipe

Source: vignettes/book-05-recipe.Rmd
book-05-recipe.Rmd

What you will learn

Build education and cause-of-death columns, check language 2, and request category counts.

This chapter uses the synthetic practice connection from Getting started. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Select the education question

An event describes records of interest. It is a definition on your computer, not a downloaded table. Start with the question from chapter 4:

education_event <- omop_event("observation", concepts = 900001L)
class(education_event)
#> [1] "omop_event" "list"

The server will select observations whose question is Education question.

Choose one answer per person

A reducer turns possibly many records into one value. Use the latest nonmissing coded answer, ordered by the observation date:

education <- omop_variable(
  event = education_event,
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"))
class(education)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

This makes one categorical column. It does not create a separate binary column for every education level. A same-date tie uses the documented deterministic record ordering; it does not mean “largest answer ID”.

Add cause of death 

cause <- omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("death"),
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", value = "cause_concept_id"))
class(cause)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

Here the value comes from cause_concept_id. Do not substitute cause_source_value: that is free source text, not the curated coded cause used by this route.

Describe a wide table

Wide means one column per variable. Person grain means one row per person. The native all-person population retains people who have neither answer nor death.

people <- omop_recipe(
  variables = list(education = education, cause_of_death = cause),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
class(people)
#> [1] "omop_recipe" "list"

person_id is included automatically as a pseudonym. Missing records produce missing values. We did not add a legacy raw-ID variable to keep the roster.

Check the language before running 

explained <- recipe_explain(people, conns = conns)
stopifnot(explained$selected == "v2")
explained$selected
#> [1] "v2"

The selected plan is language 2. This check is made for every executable recipe in the book. To read all the chosen defaults, print the explanation:

recipe_explain(people)
#> Recipe plan (language 2.0, semantic 2.0.0)
#> Population 'base' (criteria): none
#> Variables:
#>   education: last_value of event 'obs_900001' (value 'value_as_concept_id') over any time; missing = "skip"
#>   cause_of_death: first_value of event 'death' (value 'cause_concept_id') over any time; missing = "skip"
#> Output 'people' [wide] rows 'base', grain person
#> Published: people
#> Defaults relied on:
#>   - variable 'education': rows with a NULL value are skipped before the row is selected (missing = "skip")
#>   - variable 'cause_of_death': rows with a NULL value are skipped before the row is selected (missing = "skip")
#> Concept presentation: factors; identity is the declared concept class, preserved through aliases and value-preserving reducers.
#> Label precedence: variable recode, recipe recode, vocabulary name, decimal ID fallback. Explicit equal recodes merge categories.
#> Federation: permitted ID union, including declared unused levels; newest comparable vocabulary version, then bytewise name tie. Unresolved versions never establish recency.
#> Generated names: ASCII snake_case vocabulary tokens; colliding automatic names gain concept-ID suffixes. Vocabulary-dependent names are unresolved until permitted federation reconciliation.
#> variables.education: concept origin follows reducer last_value over value_as_concept_id; explicit variable name is retained.
#> variables.cause_of_death: concept origin follows reducer first_value over cause_concept_id; explicit variable name is retained.

With no time restriction, each variable reads all available history independently. That is a teaching definition, not an assumption to carry silently into a study.

Assign the result 

print(recipe_execute(people, out = c(people = "D_people"), conns = conns))
#>     people 
#> "D_people"

The reply is a mapping of output names to server symbols. D_people is still on the server. Concept-valued columns are labelled factors because of their declared type. In 2.10.4 the names education and cause_of_death need no _concept_id suffix.

Count the education categories 

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_people$education", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
#> $output.list
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_row.props
#>                       study
#> D_people$education     site
#>   Secondary education     1
#>   University education    1
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_col.props
#>                       study
#> D_people$education     site
#>   Secondary education   0.5
#>   University education  0.5
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_counts
#>                       study
#> D_people$education     site
#>   Secondary education     6
#>   University education    6
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_proportions
#> D_people$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                  0.5                  0.5 
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_people$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6 
#> 
#> 
#> $validity.message
#> [1] "Data in all studies were valid"

The labels are names, not numeric codes. useNA = "no" excludes missing answers; the counts therefore need not add up to the whole population. DataSHIELD checks whether cells may be released before returning the table.

Count causes 

ds.omop.table("D_people", "cause_of_death", conns = conns)
#> D_people$cause_of_death
#> Myocardial infarction             Pneumonia 
#>                    12                     6

ds.omop.table() calls the real dsBase ds.table() and preserves the complete published category contract, including declared zero categories. It also protects labels containing punctuation. Prefer it when you need that complete contract.

Give a question your own yes/no labels 

fever <- omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("observation", concepts = 900002L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"),
  labels = c("900301" = "yes", "900302" = "no"))
class(fever)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

The map is keyed by answer concepts. It changes presentation, not which question is selected. Missing fever answers remain missing; they do not become “no”.

answers <- omop_recipe(
  variables = list(education = education, fever = fever, cause_of_death = cause),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(answers, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(answers, out = c(people = "D_answers"), conns = conns))
#>      people 
#> "D_answers"
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_answers$fever", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
#> $output.list
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_row.props
#>                study
#> D_answers$fever site
#>             yes    1
#>             no     1
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_col.props
#>                study
#> D_answers$fever site
#>             yes  0.5
#>             no   0.5
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_counts
#>                study
#> D_answers$fever site
#>             yes    6
#>             no     6
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_proportions
#> D_answers$fever
#> yes  no 
#> 0.5 0.5 
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_answers$fever
#> yes  no 
#>   6   6 
#> 
#> 
#> $validity.message
#> [1] "Data in all studies were valid"

The table contains your lower-case labels. See the short harmonisation appendix for the same operation across two different vocabularies.

Recap

An event selects records, a reducer selects a value, and a wide output arranges private rows. Only the aggregate returns to you.

Try it

Count education using the complete-contract helper instead of calling ds.table directly.

Solution

ds.omop.table("D_people", "education", conns = conns)
#> D_people$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6
